Title: Diagnosis
Details: The issue is related to the union operation in the XPath node-set implementation not sorting the resulting nodes in document order. The test case `testUnion()` expects the union of two node sets ("/vendor[1]/contact[4]" and "/vendor[1]/contact[1]") to return nodes sorted in document order so the string value of the first node in the union is correct. The current bug report clarifies this and shows that according to the XPath specification, when a node-set is converted to a string, the string value of the node that appears first in document order must be returned. The incorrect value returned indicates that the union operation returns nodes unordered or in a wrong order.

Looking at the relevant code, the method `compareNodePointers` performs comparison of nodes by walking up their parent pointers to a common ancestor and then uses `compareChildNodePointers` to determine element order among siblings. This method throws an exception if nodes are from different trees. This comparison routine is critical to sorting nodes according to document order.

Despite this, the failing test and bug report indicate that the union operation that produces the combined node set does not correctly use this comparison to sort the combined nodes. The lack of a proper sorting step or incorrect ordering logic in the union operation results in nodes returned out of document order and thus wrong string value results. The recent bug reports about pointer comparison exceptions confirms that pointer comparison is delicate and critical for ordering.

In summary, the root cause is that the core union operation that merges two node sets is missing or incorrectly applying document order sorting. The sorting depends on `compareNodePointers` implemented in `NodePointer` and the specific child pointer comparison logic. This leads to the node set returned by union being incorrectly ordered, causing the string conversion to pick a wrong node’s string value. Fixing the union operation to properly sort nodes using these pointer comparisons will resolve the issue.

Next step: Inspect the union method that merges node sets and verify whether it performs sorting using node pointer comparisons. If missing or incorrect, add or fix sorting logic.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
